## Your Turn:

Research question: Can we correctly classify whether an exoplanet is a Super Earth or Gas Giant?

Here's the source for the data: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/adityamishraml/nasaexoplanets

> Load in the `nasa_exoplanets.csv`

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
exoplanets <- read.csv("./data/nasa_exoplanets.csv")
```

Here are some descriptions of the variables of interest:

+   `name` (character): name of planet by NASA

+   `distance` (numeric): distance of the planet from Earth in light years

+   `stellar_magnitude` (numeric): brightness of the planet (lower number = brighter)

+   `planet_type` (character): *type of planet (Neptune-like, Gas Giant, Super Earth)*

+   `discovery_year` (numeric): year in which planet got discovered

+   `mass_multiplier` (numeric): mass multiplier with respect to the planet in `mass_wrt`

+   `mass_wrt` (character): planet in our solar system in which the mass of the exoplanet is compared to (Neptune, Jupiter, Earth, respectively)

+   `radius_multiplier` (numeric): radius multiplier with respect to the planet in `mass_wrt`

+   `radius_wrt` (character): planet in our solar system in which the radius of the exoplanet is compared to (Neptune, Jupiter, Earth, respectively)

+   `orbital_radius` (numeric): radial distance the exoplanet takes around its sun in astronomical units

+   `orbital_period` (numeric): time in years it takes the exoplanet to go around its sun

+   `eccentricity` (numeric): how circular the exoplanet's orbital path is around the sun (values close to zero equaling circular)

+   `detection_method` (character): method used to detect the planet (Transit, Radial Velocity)

> Check the balance of your outcome: `planet_type`

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
table(exoplanets$planet_type)
```

> Subset `planet_type` based on our research question (see above loading the data)

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Need to subset for Super Earths and Gas Giants
exo_subset <- exoplanets[
  exoplanets$planet_type %in% c("Super Earth", "Gas Giant"),
]
```

> Are the outcomes balanced?

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Obtain frequency of outcomes
outcome_freq <- table(exo_subset$planet_type)

# Obtain proportions
outcome_freq / sum(outcome_freq)
```

Quite balanced.

> Do the following:

+   Remove the variables `names` and `detection_method`

+   Set your outcome to a factor with levels: Super Earth and Gas Giant (in that order!)

    +   Set the `*_wrt` variables to factors in the same pattern of levels (Earth and Jupiter)

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Remove variables
exo_voi <- exo_subset[,-c(1, 13)]

# Set factors
## I plan to set Super Earth = 0 and Gas Giant = 1,
## I will want to set up these factors in the same way
exo_voi$planet_type <- factor(exo_voi$planet_type, levels = c("Super Earth", "Gas Giant"))
exo_voi$mass_wrt <- factor(exo_voi$mass_wrt, levels = c("Earth", "Jupiter"))
exo_voi$radius_wrt <- factor(exo_voi$radius_wrt, levels = c("Earth", "Jupiter"))
```

> Perform logistic regression using all variables to predict `planet_type`

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Perform logistic regression
model <- glm(planet_type ~ ., family = "binomial", data = exo_voi)

# # Check mulitcollinearity
# vif(model)
# Looped over to determine variables to keep

# Keep variables
keep <- !(colnames(exo_voi) %in% c("mass_wrt", "radius_wrt", "orbital_radius"))

# Removed variables:
# 1. `mass_wrt` = highest VIF
# 2. `radius_wrt` = next highest VIF
# 3. `orbital_radius` = next highest VIF
model <- glm(
  planet_type ~ ., family = "binomial", 
  data = exo_voi[,keep]
); summary(model)
```

> Cycle through the following steps until your results satisfy multicollinearity

+   Check for multicollinearity and handle any issues (use `Std. Error` to guide you)

+   Re-estimate model

+   Repeat until you have your final model

> Final model

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Subset to final data
exo_final <- exo_voi[,keep]

# Final model
final_model <- glm(planet_type ~ ., family = "binomial", data = exo_final)
summary(final_model)
```

> Show that your model satisfies multicollinearity

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Check multicollinearity
vif(final_model)
```

> Compute the pseudo-$R^2$

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# McFadden's R-squared
PseudoR2(final_model)
```

> Compute the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and kappa of your predictions (hint: you'll need to subset your original data!)

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Get predictions
predictions <- predict(final_model, type = "response")

# Convert probabilities to predicted classes
classes <- factor(
  ifelse(predictions > 0.50, "Gas Giant", "Super Earth"),
  levels = c("Super Earth", "Gas Giant")
) # P(Y = 1 | X) = Gas Giant

# There are missing data so a prediction cannot be made
# unless the missing data are removed
exo_final <- na.omit(exo_final)

# Print confusion matrix
confusionMatrix(
  data = classes, # predictions
  reference = exo_final$planet_type, # actual
  positive = "Gas Giant" 
)
```

> Create a mosaic plot

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, comment = NA, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Create mosaic table
mosaic_table <- table(
  prediction = classes,
  actual = exo_final$planet_type
)

# Print out the table
mosaic_table

# Next we can input this into the mosaicplot() function in base R
mosaicplot(
  mosaic_table, main = 'Confusion Matrix', 
  xlab = 'actual', ylab = 'prediction',
  color = '#824670', border = "#F7B32B"
)
```
